cues.text: Customers and tailors use special words. Here are the ones you will hear the most.
Hem. The bottom edge of pants, a skirt, or a dress. To hem it means to make it shorter.
Taper. Make the pant leg narrower, usually from the knee down.
Inseam. The length of the inside of the leg, from the crotch seam to the bottom.
Break. The small fold where the bottom of the pants touches the shoe.
Take in. Make it smaller or tighter, like the waist of pants.
Let out. Make it bigger. This only works if there is extra fabric hidden inside the seam.
Seam. The line where two pieces of fabric are sewn together.
Dart. A small sewn fold that gives shape, often on blouses, dresses, and pants.
Use these words on the ticket. If the customer says shorter, write hem. If they say tighter, write take in. Then the tailor knows exactly what to do.
